description: Keep Salesforce up to date from your workflows: create and update leads, accounts, contacts and opportunities, and log follow-up tasks.

salesforce_new_contact_trigger.description: Runs for each new contact in Salesforce, including one made by converting a lead. Contacts already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.AccountId: The record ID of the account they belong to.
output.LastModifiedDate: When the contact was last changed.
output.MailingCity: The city of their mailing address.
output.MailingCountry: The country of their mailing address.
output.Name: Their full name.
output.Title: Their job title.

salesforce_new_lead_trigger.description: Runs for each new lead in Salesforce, from a web form, an import, a person or another app. Leads already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.IsConverted: Whether the lead has been converted.
output.LastModifiedDate: When the lead was last changed.
output.LeadSource: Where the lead came from, such as Web.
output.Name: Their full name.
output.Status: The lead's status, such as Open - Not Contacted.
output.Title: Their job title.

salesforce_new_opportunity_trigger.description: Runs for each new opportunity (deal) in Salesforce. Opportunities already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.AccountId: The record ID of its account.
output.CloseDate: When it is expected to close.
output.IsClosed: Whether it is closed, won or lost.
output.Name: The opportunity's name.
output.Probability: How likely it is to close, in percent.
output.StageName: The stage it is in, such as Prospecting.
output.Type: Its type, such as New Customer.

salesforce_new_record_trigger.description: Runs for each new record of the object you choose, such as an account, a case or one of your org's own objects, with its fields by their API names. Records already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.Name: Its name, for an object that has one.
output.OwnerId: The record ID of its owner, for an object that has one.

parameters.description: What kind of record to watch, such as Account, Case or one of your org's own objects.
parameters.name: object_type

salesforce_opportunity_stage_changed_tri.description: Runs when an opportunity moves to a new stage in Salesforce, or only when it moves to the stage you choose, such as Closed Won. A deal that moves on and back again runs it again. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.AccountId: The record ID of its account.
output.CloseDate: When it is expected to close.
output.IsClosed: Whether it is closed, won or lost.
output.Name: The opportunity's name.
output.Probability: How likely it is to close, in percent.
output.StageName: The stage it is in, such as Prospecting.
output.Type: Its type, such as New Customer.

parameters.description: Only run when an opportunity moves to this stage, written as it appears in Salesforce, such as Closed Won. Leave blank to run for every move.
parameters.name: stage_name

salesforce_updated_record_trigger.description: Runs each time a record of the object you choose is changed in Salesforce, such as an account, a case or one of your org's own objects, with its fields as they are now. A new record doesn't run it until it is changed. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.Name: Its name, for an object that has one.
output.OwnerId: The record ID of its owner, for an object that has one.

parameters.description: What kind of record to watch, such as Account, Case or one of your org's own objects.
parameters.name: object_type
